title: Negative (first probe of Q:metabolic-crawler-setpoint): doubling rim uptake grows the metabolic crawler 3x to a saturating size (area 2.3 -> 6.7, rising only 0.27 over the last 13 t) but it stays one cell with one front; no front splitting or fission by t=60
summary: world.py of 20261025T2238-c22-metabolic-crawler-regrowth with SYN_RIM=1, ksyn=0.2 (2x), kdeg=0.1, rn=0.25, box L=6 at N=300, seed 0, t=60 (probe image rim_ksyn02_s0.png, track rim_ksyn02_s0_track.txt). The crawler's area rises from 2.27 to 6.71 and saturates (6.44 at t=45, 6.71 at t=58.5). That fits a set size from rim uptake against whole-body decay, now at ~2.6x the ksyn=0.1 size. The polarized area stays 1.6-1.8 as the cell grows, so the front is a narrowing fraction of a larger crescent, and the speed rises from 0.41 to 0.47. No second front appears, and the cell never divides. So feeding alone makes a bigger crawler, not two; division would need a size-triggered front instability, which this polarity does not supply at rho*=0.2. One seed, one feeding level, probe only.
